description: §6.8.4 (RT) — an IMPLICITLY declared cell (`@x = 0`, no `<x>` declaration) written TWICE at module-init, with `tare(@x)` between the writes. `tare` promotes the init expression live at that point into the cell's reset default, so reset(@x) restores 0 rather than re-running the second write's `current + 1`. This is the FIRST-write intent; the last-write intent has its own case (tare-last-write-baseline-rt) over structurally identical source.
rationale: §6.8.4: `default=` is an ATTRIBUTE and needs a declaration site, which an implicitly declared cell has none of, so before this amendment such a cell could not say what it returns to — the last write's init thunk always won and reset INCREMENTED. `tare` gives the cell the same reach into the default slot from a statement, and §6.8.2's default-before-init precedence does the rest. The compiler deliberately performs NO static analysis of which write is the baseline; source position is the discriminator.
